answer: Reputation escrow makes sybil attacks expensive: an agent must lock a refundable stake before it can trade, and peers slash that stake when they attest fraud. A whisper network of signed attestations spreads fraud reports faster than new fake identities can be spun up, so a hollow identity with no history and no stake earns no trust and no work. Even at the nadir of a market, when honest work is scarce, forfeiting stakes across many identities costs more than faking volume can ever return.
